numerical_failure.observed_behavior: np.quantile with all-zero weights (method='inverted_cdf') returns the first sample instead of raising; the cdf normalization cdf /= cdf[-1, ...] emits a RuntimeWarning 'invalid value encountered in divide' and the result is array(1).
numerical_failure.expected_behavior: np.quantile should raise an error (ValueError) when weights are all zeros, and also when at least one weight is np.nan or np.inf; the fix raises ValueError with message 'Weights included NaN, inf or were all zero.'
trigger_conditions: weights contain np.nan or np.inf (expected to raise as well)

input_output_examples.buggy_output: RuntimeWarning: invalid value encountered in divide; returns array(1)

oracle_clues: RuntimeWarning 'invalid value encountered in divide' at cdf /= cdf[-1, ...]
fix raises ValueError with message 'Weights included NaN, inf or were all zero.'
tests use pytest.raises(ValueError) and check message substring 'Weights must be non-infinite' in proposed discussion tests

category_specific_evidence: Issue #28589 reproducer: np.quantile([1,2,3,4], 0.5, weights=[0,0,0,0], method='inverted_cdf') previously produced a RuntimeWarning 'invalid value encountered in divide' at cdf /= cdf[-1, ...] and returned array(1) instead of erroring.
The division cdf /= cdf[-1] with all-zero weights yields NaN (0/0), so the normalization-to-1 property of the weight CDF is violated silently.
PR #28595 states quantile should raise errors when all weights are zero, when any weight is np.nan, or when any weight is np.inf.
The patch adds a check after cdf normalization: if np.isnan(cdf[-1]).any() then raise ValueError('Weights included NaN, inf or were all zero.')
Review discussion suggests parametrizing tests over np.quantile and np.percentile, which should raise the same errors, and over dtype=float and dtype=object for list inputs.
reproduction_risks: The passages do not state the exact expected output after the fix beyond raising ValueError; the reproducer's prior output array(1) is the buggy value, not a verified correct value.
Whether the NaN/inf weight cases produce the same warning path was not demonstrated with concrete values in the passages.
